summary.text: Terri DeBoer, a Republican and longtime West Michigan television meteorologist, lost the November 3, 2026 election for U.S. House in Michigan's 3rd District to Hillary Scholten.

paragraphs.text: Terri DeBoer was born at Fort Dix, New Jersey, and raised in a military family, according to her campaign website; she earned a high school diploma from C.M. Russell High School.
She told Fox News she became interested in politics after hearing Ronald Reagan speak in person during her senior year of high school.
DeBoer began in broadcast journalism as a news reporter before moving to meteorology in the early 1990s, according to Fox News.
She has forecast weather on West Michigan television for more than 30 years, at WWMT-TV, WOOD-TV and FOX-17 (WXMI), where she returned in 2024 and left in early 2026.
DeBoer has been inducted into the Michigan Emmy Silver Circle, and her campaign website also describes her as an author.
She has served on the boards of the Mental Health Foundation of West Michigan and the Grand Rapids Griffins Youth Foundation, and on the Millennium Park Commission.
She lives in Byron Center and describes herself as a wife, mother and grandmother.
DeBoer announced her candidacy in March 2026 and won the August 4, 2026 Republican primary with 78.6% of the vote over Ryan Cushman.
During the campaign, she described herself as an outsider and said her priorities included lowering the cost of living, securing the border and community safety.
She received 41.4% of the vote to Hillary Scholten's 57.1%, according to unofficial results reported by NBC News.
